walkthroughs.body_html:
Principles of Chemistry — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Principles of Chemistry brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Principles of Chemistry.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The electron configuration of sodium (atomic number 11) is:
The bond formed when two non-metal atoms share a pair of electrons is:
options: Covalent
Ionic
Metallic
Intermolecular

mcqs.q: In which state of matter do particles only vibrate about fixed positions?
options: Solid
Liquid
Gas
Aqueous solution

mcqs.q: An atom with 17 protons and 18 neutrons has a mass number of:
Do particles get bigger when a substance is heated?
options: Heating makes the particles multiply, increasing the volume.
Isotopes differ only in their number of electrons.
Heating makes each particle swell up, which is why materials expand.
No — the particles stay the same size; they gain energy, move faster and spread further apart, so the substance expands.

mcqs.q: Does sodium chloride exist as NaCl molecules?
options: No — it forms a giant lattice of alternating Na⁺ and Cl⁻ ions; the formula NaCl gives only the ratio of ions.
NaCl is a molecule made of one sodium atom joined to one chlorine atom.
Sodium chloride is made of free-floating single atoms.
Heating makes the particles multiply, increasing the volume.

mcqs.q: Are isotopes of an element different elements?
options: Adding neutrons changes the element, so isotopes are different elements.
No — isotopes are atoms of the same element with the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Sodium chloride is made of free-floating single atoms.
Isotopes differ only in their number of electrons.
